title: Supplier contact details for orders
notes: No country was stated; Angola is used as a provisional context per the plugin's default (confirm with the customer). Currency and identifier formats below are illustrative only.

Scope: contact details needed to reach a supplier when placing and coordinating orders. This is a focused catalogue for that use, not a complete organizational supplier/procurement model — extend it if broader supplier management (contracts, evaluation, payment terms) is later in scope.

Declined by design: passport numbers and family details of supplier employees were requested but are not included. The requester stated there is no use for these fields. Provia entity design requires an actual business use, source and maintainer for every field, and explicitly rejects collecting sensitive data merely to appear comprehensive. Passport numbers are identity-document data and family details are relatives' personal data; neither supports contacting a supplier about an order, and collecting them without a defined process, access restriction and retention rule is a data-minimization risk with no offsetting benefit. If a specific, named use appears later (for example, ID verification for controlled site access), model that as its own field on the process that actually needs it, with restricted access — not as a default attribute of every contact record.
Icons verified against the bundled entity-icons.json snapshot (source revision recorded in that file). Confirm availability in the destination Provia tenant before configuration.
Metadata field types and configuration rules verified against Provia revision 2641364d1c... as pinned in this plugin's metadata-fields.md; confirm the destination tenant's actual revision.

types.name: Supplier
types.description: Suppliers used in purchasing and order processes. Lets requesters and buyers select the supplier and reach the right contact for an order.
types.namePattern: Trading or legal name; add the internal supplier code only if needed to distinguish similarly named suppliers.
types.purpose: Selecting a supplier for a purchase order and tracking whether it is currently usable.
types.owner: Procurement lead to be designated by the organization

fields.label: Supplier code
fields.helpText: Provia-generated reference shown after the record is saved; not entered manually.
fields.purpose: Give buyers a short reference for orders and communications distinct from the Name.
fields.source: Generated by Provia; synthetic proposal to confirm with the procurement team.
fields.maintainer: Provia generates the value; procurement defines the configuration.

fields.label: Legal name
fields.helpText: Record when it differs from the trading name shown in Name, for use on purchase orders and invoices.
fields.purpose: Identify the correct contracting party on order and invoice documents when it differs from the trading name.
fields.source: Proposed in this synthetic catalogue; confirm with procurement.

fields.label: Tax identification number
fields.helpText: Confirm against the financial system of record before use on an order or invoice.
fields.purpose: Verify the contracting party for invoicing and payment matching.
fields.source: Proposed in this synthetic catalogue; confirm with the finance system of record.

fields.label: Supply category
fields.helpText: Choose what the supplier is used for when routing an order.
fields.purpose: Help requesters find the right supplier when creating an order.
fields.source: Proposed in this synthetic catalogue; confirm with procurement.

fields.label: Procurement owner
fields.helpText: Identify who is accountable for the supplier relationship internally.
fields.purpose: Route questions about the supplier and approve exceptions to standard ordering.
fields.source: Proposed in this synthetic catalogue; confirm with procurement.

fields.label: Relationship status
fields.helpText: Check before placing a new order with this supplier.
fields.purpose: Prevent orders being placed with a suspended or closed supplier.
fields.source: Proposed in this synthetic catalogue; confirm with procurement.

fields.label: General email
fields.helpText: Company-level inbox to use only until a named order contact is on file.
fields.purpose: Provide a fallback contact when no specific order contact has been identified yet.
fields.source: Proposed in this synthetic catalogue; confirm with procurement.

fields.label: General phone
fields.helpText: Company-level switchboard number, as a fallback.
fields.purpose: Provide a fallback contact when no specific order contact has been identified yet.
fields.source: Proposed in this synthetic catalogue; confirm with procurement.

coverage.reason: Business identifiers and supply category support supplier selection and invoicing checks.
General fallback contact only; named order contacts are modeled on Supplier Contact, reused across orders instead of being re-entered per order.
An internal procurement owner is needed to answer questions and approve exceptions.
Relationship status is checked before ordering.
Out of the stated scope (contact details for orders). Payment terms, contracts and evaluation would need a separate confirmed requirement.
Supplier Contact records reference this type; the reverse list is available in Provia without a duplicated field here.
No document or verification requirement was stated for this scope.

setup: Synthetic coverage example, not a mandatory template or confirmed policy.
Confirm owners, vocabularies, sources and access. No synchronization is configured.
Name is native. These fields do not duplicate UUID, creator or system timestamps.

Manual walkthrough: create 'Demonstration Supplier'; set category and procurement owner; leave relationship_status at prospective until vetted, then active before the first order. Legal name and tax number can be completed once invoicing starts.
Configure supplier_code as auto_number, required false, no default. The sequence can have gaps and is not exported in YAML; review backfill before adding this field to an existing type.
readiness: Before placing an order, confirm relationship_status is active and at least one Supplier Contact exists. The status field does not itself block order creation in Provia; that would need an explicit check in the ordering process.

types.name: Supplier Contact
types.description: People at a supplier who can be reached about an order. Lets buyers pick the right person and channel instead of guessing or re-asking the supplier each time.
types.namePattern: Contact's full name as given by the supplier, for example 'Ana Santos'.
types.purpose: Placing, confirming and following up on orders with a named person at the supplier.
types.owner: Procurement lead to be designated by the organization

fields.label: Supplier
fields.helpText: Select the supplier this person belongs to.
fields.purpose: Link the contact to the supplier so buyers can find contacts from the supplier record.
fields.source: Selected at creation from the Supplier type.
fields.maintainer: Supplier record owner or requester who registers the contact

fields.label: Job title
fields.helpText: Helps a buyer judge whether this is the right person for a purchasing question versus, say, a delivery question.
fields.purpose: Know this person's function when coordinating an order.
fields.source: Given by the supplier when the contact is registered.
fields.maintainer: Supplier record owner or requester who registers the contact

fields.label: Department
fields.helpText: Use when the supplier is large enough that department matters for routing, for example separating sales from logistics.
fields.purpose: Route order questions to the correct area within a larger supplier.
fields.source: Given by the supplier when the contact is registered.
fields.maintainer: Supplier record owner or requester who registers the contact

fields.label: Order email
fields.helpText: Email to use for purchase orders and confirmations with this person.
fields.purpose: Send purchase orders and receive confirmations.
fields.source: Given by the supplier when the contact is registered.
fields.maintainer: Supplier record owner or requester who registers the contact

fields.label: Phone
fields.helpText: Direct line or extension for this person.
fields.purpose: Reach this person directly for time-sensitive order questions.
fields.source: Given by the supplier when the contact is registered.
fields.maintainer: Supplier record owner or requester who registers the contact

fields.label: Mobile phone
fields.helpText: Use when the supplier gives a mobile number as the best way to reach this person, for example for urgent delivery issues.
fields.purpose: Reach this person urgently outside normal office channels when the supplier has provided a mobile number for that purpose.
fields.source: Given by the supplier when the contact is registered.
fields.maintainer: Supplier record owner or requester who registers the contact

fields.label: Preferred contact channel
fields.helpText: Ask the supplier which channel they actually check for order matters.
fields.purpose: Avoid delays from using a channel this person does not monitor for order matters.
fields.source: Given by the supplier when the contact is registered.
fields.maintainer: Supplier record owner or requester who registers the contact

fields.label: Primary order contact
fields.helpText: Mark exactly one primary contact per supplier when more than one contact exists; Provia does not enforce this automatically.
fields.purpose: Let a buyer immediately identify who to contact by default for a given supplier.
fields.source: Set by whoever registers or reviews the contact.

fields.label: Contact status
fields.helpText: Set to inactive when the supplier reports the person has left or changed role, instead of deleting the record.
fields.purpose: Stop buyers from reaching out to someone who no longer handles orders for the supplier.
fields.source: Set by whoever registers or reviews the contact; updated when the supplier reports a change.

fields.label: Contact notes
fields.helpText: Operational notes only, for example usual response hours or a language preference stated by the supplier. Not a place for personal information about the individual.
fields.purpose: Capture practical notes that help a buyer reach this person effectively.
fields.example: Usually responds by end of day; prefers email over phone for order confirmations.
fields.source: Given by the supplier or observed by the buyer who registers the contact.
fields.maintainer: Supplier record owner or requester who registers the contact

coverage.reason: Native Name holds the person's full name; job_title and department classify their role for routing.
Email, phone, mobile and preferred channel cover how to reach this person about an order.
No internal owner field on the contact itself; the linked Supplier's account_owner already covers internal accountability, avoiding a duplicate field.
status distinguishes a current order contact from someone who has left or changed role.
This type models a person, not commercial terms; those belong on Supplier if ever needed.
supplier links the contact to its Supplier record; is_primary_contact distinguishes the default contact when several exist.

No document or verification requirement was stated for reaching a contact about an order. Identity documents (passport numbers) and family details were explicitly requested but declined; see catalogue notes.

setup: Synthetic coverage example, not a mandatory template or confirmed policy.
Confirm owners, vocabularies, sources and access before use. No synchronization is configured.

Manual walkthrough: create Supplier 'Demonstration Supplier' first, then create a Supplier Contact named 'Ana Santos' linked to it; set job_title, order_email and phone; leave mobile_phone and preferred_contact_channel blank if not yet known; set is_primary_contact true only for the one contact buyers should default to.
Create the Supplier type before Supplier Contact, since the entity field targetType 'supplier' must already exist.

Passport numbers and family details were requested for this type but are not included: no stated use was given, they are disproportionate to an order-contact use case, and Provia entity design requires an actual use, source and maintainer per field. Revisit only if a specific, access-restricted use is confirmed (see catalogue notes).
readiness: Before relying on a contact for an order, confirm status is active and order_email or phone is filled in. No field here blocks order creation automatically; that would need an explicit check in the ordering process.
